---
title: "Maps"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 6,
  dpi = 72,
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

```{r}
library(plot2)
```

Geographic data of class `sf`, from the [`sf` package](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/), become maps in `plot2()`. This article uses the data set `netherlands`, which contains the twelve provinces of the Netherlands with their area:

```{r}
netherlands
```

## A first map

Without other arguments, the first numeric column becomes the `category` and the first character column becomes the data labels. The labels are placed at the centre of each area:

```{r}
netherlands |>
  plot2()
```

For maps, `plot2()` removes the axes, places the legend on the right and uses a continuous colour scale for a numeric `category`.

## Category and colours

`category` accepts a column or a calculation, as for other data:

```{r}
netherlands |>
  plot2(category = ifelse(area_km2 > 3000, "Larger than 3 000 km²", "Smaller"),
        colour_fill = c("#4E79A7", "#E8E8E8"),
        category.title = "Area")
```

`colour_fill` sets the colours of the areas and `colour` sets the colour of the borders. The options `plot2.colour_sf_fill` and `plot2.colour_sf` set their defaults for all maps.

## Data labels

`datalabels` sets the text of the labels, or removes them with `datalabels = FALSE`:

```{r}
netherlands |>
  plot2(category = area_km2,
        category.title = "Area (km²)",
        datalabels = paste0(province, "\n", round(area_km2), " km²"),
        datalabels.size = 2.5,
        colour_fill = "mako")
```

The labels are placed at the centre of each area (`sf::st_centroid()`). For areas with an irregular shape, the centre can lie outside the area; `datalabels.centroid = FALSE` places the labels at a point that is always on the area (`sf::st_point_on_surface()`).

## Coordinate reference system

`crs` transforms the data to another coordinate reference system with `sf::st_transform()`. The data set `netherlands` uses the Dutch national grid (EPSG:28992); this map uses the global longitude and latitude system (EPSG:4326):

```{r}
netherlands |>
  plot2(crs = 4326, datalabels = FALSE)
```

## Adding layers

`add_sf()` adds another layer of `sf` data to a map, for example to outline a selection of areas:

```{r}
northern_provinces <- netherlands[netherlands$province %in% c("Groningen", "Friesland", "Drenthe"), ]

netherlands |>
  plot2(datalabels = FALSE, colour_fill = "mako") |>
  add_sf(northern_provinces,
         colour = "#F28E2B",
         colour_fill = NA,
         linewidth = 1,
         datalabels = province)
```

The result is a `ggplot` object, so `ggplot2::geom_sf()` and other `ggplot2` functions can be added as well.
